No, my GI bill is the old one and that all goes into school. The old one is the Montgomery GI Bill, MGIB. Using the MGIB first allows you to sign up for an extra year under the new Post-9/11 GIB(which is the one that gives you cash for rent/bullshit) thus giving an extra year for veterans as we usually need it to "catch up".

But I "earn" $500/month for renting out my spare bedroom to a good friend. Any time I'm not doing homework (rare in STEM), I end up having to do some sort of maintenance (can't pay for that shit on $500/month) to keep my 1930's house (or my car) from falling apart, fighting the VA bureaucracy, or handling some other bullshit (usually either VA or school related) that pops up.

Since I own a house I can't get any food stamps or other such help. And since I rent out and have a house and go to school on the MGIB my taxes, while very small, are more complex than I would like.

The only thing I have keeping me from being just another homeless vet is the fact that I planned ahead and saved money before I got out and bought my house in cash, and my friend living with me(who would also be a homeless vet without me). If it wasn't for that I would be living in my wagon instead of just spending too much time in it to commute. It's not a particularly bad life(I've lived much worse), it just doesn't have much going for it and I have to be working on something nearly constantly to keep everything from snowballing on my ass. One disaster and it all goes away.

Ahh, I paid for the MGIB in BMT and they switched to the Post 9/11 one while I was still active. Sorry to hear of your struggles man, I definitely had it easier being paid BAH while in college. The Post 9/11 GI Bill is actually pretty amazing and I will recommend my children do it if they want to go to college, even though I could probably afford to pay their way. 4 years of active duty and learning a lot while serving and you get rewarded with 4 years of being paid ~$1000/month plus tuition for college is a deal I don't think anyone should pass up. It was the best experience of my life and I met my wife while in the military. I think everything about it made me a better and more confident person, and it also taught me about life and introduced me to a broad range of people from many different backgrounds. It also pushed me pretty far into the Libertarian realm of politics seeing just how much waste happens with government contracting, but that is a topic for a different day I think.

Good on you for doing what you have to do to make a better life for yourself and good luck with your degree. Thanks for your service and I hope all of your hard work pays off soon.
